rows.stem:
\(\mathrm{Zn + 2CH_3COOH \longrightarrow (CH_3COO)_2\,Zn + H_2}\)

The above reaction is a :
rows.solution:
Zinc is more reactive than hydrogen, so it takes the place of hydrogen in ethanoic acid, forming zinc ethanoate and setting hydrogen free:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2CH_3COOH \rightarrow (CH_3COO)_2Zn + H_2}\)

One element displacing another from its compound is a displacement reaction. This is option (B) Displacement reaction.

rows.stem: An aqueous solution of a salt turns blue litmus to red. The salt could be the one obtained by the reaction of :
rows.solution:
A salt whose solution turns blue litmus red is acidic, so it must come from a strong acid and a weak base. HCl is a strong acid and \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) is a weak base, giving ammonium chloride, whose solution is acidic. Nitric acid with NaOH and sulphuric acid with KOH give neutral salts, and ethanoic acid with NaOH gives a basic salt.

This is option (D) HCl and \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Four solutions, namely glucose, alcohol, hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid filled in four separate beakers are connected one by one in an electric circuit with a bulb. The solutions in which the bulb will glow when current is passed are :
rows.solution:
The bulb glows only if the solution conducts, that is, if it contains ions. Acids give \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions in water, so hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid conduct. Glucose and alcohol contain hydrogen but do not form \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions in solution, so they do not conduct.

This is option (D) Hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid.

rows.stem: The metals which are found in both free state as well as combined state are :
rows.solution:
Metals at the bottom of the activity series, such as gold and platinum, are found only in the free state. Copper and silver are found in the free state as well as in the combined state, as their sulphide or oxide ores.

This is option (C) Copper and silver.

rows.stem: The number of single and double bonds present in a molecule of benzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\)) respectively, are :
rows.solution:
In the benzene structure the six carbon atoms form a ring with single and double bonds alternating. Counting the bonds:

single bonds: 6 C–H bonds and 3 C–C single bonds, a total of 9;

double bonds: 3 C=C bonds.

This is option (B) 9 and 3.

rows.stem: In human beings, when the process of digestion is completed, the (i) proteins, (ii) carbohydrates, and (iii) fats are respectively finally converted into :

options.label: A
options.text: (i) Amino acids, (ii) glucose and (iii) fatty acids

options.label: B
options.text: (i) Amino acids, (ii) glucose, (iii) fatty acids and glycerol

options.label: C
options.text: (i) Glucose, (ii) fatty acids and glycerol, (iii) amino acids

options.label: D
options.text: (i) Sugars, (ii) amino acids, (iii) fatty acids and glycerol

rows.solution:
At the end of digestion, proteins are broken down to amino acids, carbohydrates to glucose, and fats to fatty acids and glycerol. (Fats do not stop at fatty acids alone; glycerol is released as well.)

This is option (B) (i) Amino acids, (ii) glucose, (iii) fatty acids and glycerol.

rows.stem: A plant growth inhibitor hormone which causes wilting of leaves is called :
rows.solution:
Abscisic acid inhibits growth, and its effects include wilting of leaves. Auxin, cytokinin and gibberellin all promote growth.

This is option (C) Abscisic acid.

rows.stem: The plants that can be raised by the method of vegetative propagation are :
rows.solution:
Sugarcane, roses and grapes are grown by vegetative propagation, using methods such as layering and grafting. Every other choice includes a plant raised from seed: mustard appears in three of them, and papaya in one. (Potato, banana and orange can be raised vegetatively, but each sits beside mustard.)

This is option (A) Sugarcane, roses, grapes.

rows.stem: The part of seed which is a source of food during germination of seed is :
rows.solution:
The cotyledons are the seed leaves that store food, and the embryo uses this stored food as it germinates. The radicle grows into the root and the plumule into the shoot.

This is option (A) Cotyledon.

rows.stem: A zygote is formed by the fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete. The number of chromosomes in the zygote of a human is :
rows.solution:
Each human gamete carries 23 chromosomes. Their fusion restores the full number in the zygote: \(23 + 23 = 46\).

This is option (C) 46.

rows.stem: Absolute refractive index of glass and water is \(\frac{3}{2}\) and \(\frac{4}{3}\) respectively. If the speed of light in glass is \(2 \times 10^8\) m/s, the speed of light in water is :
rows.solution:
Speed of light in vacuum: \(c = n_g \times v_g = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2 \times 10^8 = 3 \times 10^8\) m/s.

Speed in water: \(v_w = \dfrac{c}{n_w} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{4/3} = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 10^8\) m/s.

This is option (A) \(\frac{9}{4} \times 10^8\) m/s.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: When a beam of white light passes through a region having very fine dust particles, the colour of light mainly scattered in that region is :
rows.solution:
Very fine particles scatter light of shorter wavelength much more than light of longer wavelength. Blue has the shortest wavelength of the choices, so it is scattered the most.

This is option (C) Blue.

rows.stem:
Consider the following combinations of resistors :

The combinations having equivalent resistance \(1\,\Omega\) is/are :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the four combinations I-IV are given only as drawings: I carries two 2 Ω resistors, II three 3 Ω resistors, III resistors of 2 Ω, 4 Ω, 3 Ω and 3 Ω, IV two 0·5 Ω resistors; how each set is connected (series or parallel, and which pairs share a branch) decides the equivalent resistance and is withheld here. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Work out each combination from the figure:

I: two \(2\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel: \(\dfrac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} = 1\,\Omega\).

II: three \(3\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel: \(\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = 1\), so \(R = 1\,\Omega\).

III: \(2\,\Omega\) and \(4\,\Omega\) in series (\(6\,\Omega\)) in parallel with \(3\,\Omega\) and \(3\,\Omega\) in series (\(6\,\Omega\)): \(\dfrac{6 \times 6}{6 + 6} = 3\,\Omega\).

IV: two \(0{\cdot}5\,\Omega\) resistors in parallel: \(\dfrac{0{\cdot}5}{2} = 0{\cdot}25\,\Omega\).

Only I and II give \(1\,\Omega\). This is option (C) I and II.

rows.stem: An electric iron of resistance \(20\,\Omega\) draws a current of 5 A. The heat developed in the iron in 30 seconds is :
rows.solution:
Heat produced \(H = I^2 R t = 5^2 \times 20 \times 30 = 25 \times 600 = 15000\) J.

This is option (A) 15000 J.

rows.stem: A rectangular loop ABCD carrying a current I is situated near a straight conductor XY, such that the conductor is parallel to the side AB of the loop and is in the plane of the loop. If a steady current I is established in the conductor as shown, the conductor XY will

options.label: B
options.text: move towards the side AB of the loop.

options.label: C
options.text: move away from the side AB of the loop.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the straight conductor XY (current I marked by an arrow) beside the rectangular loop ABCD (current I marked by arrows on every side, AB the side nearest XY) is given only as a drawing; the sense of the current in XY and in side AB decides attraction or repulsion and is withheld here. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
In the figure the current in XY flows upwards, and in the side AB of the loop, the side nearest XY, it also flows upwards. Two parallel conductors carrying currents in the same direction attract each other, because each lies in the magnetic field of the other and the force on it points towards the other wire. The far side CD carries current the opposite way and repels XY, but it is farther away, so its force is weaker and the attraction by AB wins.

This is option (B) move towards the side AB of the loop.

rows.stem:
Some wastes are given below :

(i) Garden waste

(ii) Ball point pen refills

(iii) Empty medicine bottles made of glass

(iv) Peels of fruits and vegetables

(v) Old cotton shirt

The non-biodegradable wastes among these are :
rows.solution:
Ball point pen refills (plastic) and glass medicine bottles cannot be broken down by bacteria and other decomposers, so they are non-biodegradable. Garden waste, peels of fruits and vegetables and an old cotton shirt are all broken down by decomposers.

This is option (B) (ii) and (iii).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The extraction of metals from their sulphide ores cannot take place without roasting of the ore.

**Reason (R) :** Roasting converts sulphide ores directly into metals.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A sulphide ore is converted into the oxide before the metal is extracted, because it is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide than from its sulphide. This conversion, by heating the ore strongly in excess air, is roasting, so the Assertion is true.

The marking scheme treats the Reason as true too. For metals low in the activity series, such as mercury and copper, heating the sulphide ore in air does end in the free metal (cinnabar gives mercury, and copper sulphide gives copper). But this does not explain why roasting is essential, so the scheme takes the Reason as true and not the correct explanation.

On a strict reading of the textbook, roasting converts a sulphide ore into an oxide (for example \(\mathrm{2ZnS + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2ZnO + 2SO_2}\)), and the metal is obtained only in a later reduction step. Read that way, the word "directly" makes the Reason false, and the answer would be that the Assertion is true while the Reason is false.

The marking scheme's answer is option (B): both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In the human heart ventricles have thicker muscular walls than atria.

**Reason (R) :** Ventricles have to pump the blood into various organs.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The ventricles have thicker muscular walls than the atria, so the Assertion is true. The ventricles have to pump blood out into the various organs of the body (and to the lungs), which needs much more force than the atria need to push blood into the ventricles next to them. The Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Magnetic field lines never intersect each other.

**Reason (R) :** If they intersect, then at the point of intersection, the compass needle would point towards two directions, which is not possible.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Magnetic field lines never intersect, so the Assertion is true. If they did, then at the point of intersection the compass needle would have to point in two directions at once, which is not possible. The Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Oxygen is essential for all aerobic forms of life.

**Reason (R) :** Free oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Oxygen is essential for all aerobic forms of life, so the Assertion is true. In the upper atmosphere free oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone, so the Reason is true as well. But the formation of ozone has nothing to do with why aerobic organisms need oxygen (they use it to break down food and release energy).

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
1 gram of solid sodium chloride was taken in a clean and dry test tube and concentrated sulphuric acid was added to it.

(i) Name the gas evolved in the reaction.

(ii) What will be observed when this gas is tested with (I) dry, and (II) wet blue litmus paper ? Write your conclusion about the nature (acidic/basic) of this gas.
rows.solution:
(i) Hydrogen chloride gas (HCl) is evolved:

\(\mathrm{NaCl + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow NaHSO_4 + HCl}\)

(ii) (I) Dry blue litmus paper shows no change in colour. (II) Wet blue litmus paper turns red.

Conclusion: HCl gas is acidic in nature. It shows its acidic behaviour only in the presence of water, because hydrogen ions are formed only when it dissolves in water.

rows.stem: Some metals react with acids to produce salt and hydrogen gas. Illustrate it with an example. How will you test the presence of this gas ?
rows.solution:
Zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to give zinc sulphate and hydrogen gas:

\(\mathrm{Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2(g)}\)

(Any other example, such as zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid, is equally good.)

Test: bring a burning matchstick (or candle) near the gas. Hydrogen burns with a pop sound.

rows.stem: Distinguish between a saturated and an unsaturated hydrocarbon by flame test. List the products of combustion reaction of a saturated hydrocarbon.
rows.solution:
Flame test: a saturated hydrocarbon burns with a clean blue flame (complete combustion). An unsaturated hydrocarbon burns with a yellow flame with lots of black smoke, a sooty flame (incomplete combustion).

Products of combustion of a saturated hydrocarbon: carbon dioxide and water, with the release of heat and light.

rows.stem: We need to water the soil in plants on a regular basis. But it ultimately reaches the leaves of the plant. Explain how this takes place.
rows.solution: Water absorbed by the roots enters the xylem, and the xylem vessels of the roots, stems and leaves are joined into one continuous channel. In the leaves, water is lost as vapour through the stomata (transpiration). This loss creates a suction, the transpiration pull, which draws water up through the xylem from the roots to the leaves.

rows.stem: Name the type of nutrition exhibited by Amoeba. Explain how food is taken in and digested by this organism.
rows.solution:
Amoeba shows heterotrophic nutrition of the holozoic type.

It takes in food using temporary finger-like extensions of the cell surface (pseudopodia), which surround the food particle and fuse over it to form a food vacuole. Inside the food vacuole, complex substances are broken down into simpler ones, which then diffuse into the cytoplasm. The undigested material is thrown out through the cell surface. (The marking scheme also accepts the steps explained with a diagram.)

rows.stem: The survival of a species is promoted through creation of variations. Illustrate with an example.
rows.solution: Variations let some individuals of a species survive when the conditions change. For example, if a population of bacteria lives in temperate waters and the water temperature rises sharply (for instance, in a heat wave caused by global warming), most of the bacteria would die. But a few variants that can withstand heat would survive and multiply. Without such variations the whole population could be wiped out, so suitable variations promote the survival of the species. (Any other suitable example is acceptable.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: A person suffering from presbyopia needs bifocal lens. If he needs two lens of power \(-4{\cdot}0\) dioptre and \(+2{\cdot}0\) dioptre, which one of these two lenses is for the correction of distant vision and what is its focal length ?
rows.solution:
The lens of power \(-4{\cdot}0\) D is a concave (diverging) lens, which corrects myopia, so it is the one used for distant vision. (The \(+2{\cdot}0\) D convex lens is for near vision.)

Its focal length is \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-4{\cdot}0} = -0{\cdot}25\) m, that is \(-25\) cm.

rows.stem: Two wires A and B of same material, having same lengths and diameters \(0{\cdot}2\) mm and \(0{\cdot}3\) mm respectively, are connected one by one in a circuit. Which one of these two wires will offer more resistance to the flow of current in the circuit ? Justify your answer.
rows.solution:
Wire A (diameter \(0{\cdot}2\) mm) will offer more resistance.

Justification: for wires of the same material and the same length, \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\), so \(R \propto \dfrac{1}{A}\). Wire A is thinner and has the smaller area of cross-section, so it has the greater resistance. (Since \(A \propto d^2\), \(\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \left(\dfrac{0{\cdot}3}{0{\cdot}2}\right)^2 = 2{\cdot}25\).)

rows.stem: Write the common name and the chemical name of the compound \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,H_2O}\). Write the method of its preparation. Give chemical equation for the reaction, when water reacts with \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,H_2O}\).
rows.solution:
Common name: Plaster of Paris. Chemical name: calcium sulphate hemihydrate.

Preparation: gypsum, \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\), is heated at 373 K. It loses water molecules and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate:

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O \xrightarrow{373\ K} CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O}\)

With water, Plaster of Paris changes back to gypsum, which sets as a hard solid mass:

\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O \rightarrow CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\)

rows.stem: Why is the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid an oxidation reaction ? Name the oxidising agent used in this conversion. Write chemical equation for this oxidation reaction. How is this reaction different from the reaction in which ethanol burns in the presence of oxygen ?
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: for the last part it also accepts that burning of ethanol is exothermic while the conversion to ethanoic acid is endothermic. The oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid also releases heat, so that contrast does not hold; the difference is the one given below.]

In this conversion oxygen is added to ethanol (and hydrogen is removed from it), so it is an oxidation reaction.

Oxidising agent: alkaline potassium permanganate, or acidified potassium dichromate, on heating.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4 \text{ + heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

Difference: this is a controlled oxidation, which stops at ethanoic acid. When ethanol burns in oxygen it undergoes combustion, a complete oxidation that gives carbon dioxide and water with the release of heat and light:

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + 3H_2O}\) + heat and light

rows.stem: Explain with the help of a labelled diagram, the process of reproduction in Hydra by budding. Name the cells used for reproduction in this process.
rows.solution:
In Hydra, a bud develops as an outgrowth because of repeated cell division at one specific site on the body. The bud grows, develops tentacles and becomes a tiny individual. When fully mature it detaches from the parent body and becomes a new independent individual.

Diagram: draw a sequence of three or four sketches of Hydra. In the first, a small bulge (the bud) appears on the side of the body; in the next, the bud is larger and has its own tentacles; in the last, the young Hydra separates from the parent. Label the tentacles and the bud.

Hydra uses its regenerative cells for reproduction by budding.

rows.stem:
List two roles of each of the following in human reproductive system :

(i) Seminal vesicles and prostate gland

(ii) Oviduct

(iii) Testis
rows.solution:
(i) Seminal vesicles and prostate gland: they add their secretions to the sperms, so that (1) the sperms are now in a fluid, which makes their transport easier, and (2) the fluid provides nutrition to the sperms.

(ii) Oviduct: (1) it carries the egg from the ovary to the womb (uterus); (2) it is the site of fertilisation.

(iii) Testis: (1) it produces sperms (the male germ cells); (2) it secretes the hormone testosterone.

rows.stem: List two differences between dominant traits and recessive traits. What percentage of pea plants in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation were with yellow seeds in Mendel’s cross between the pea plants having yellow (YY) and green coloured (yy) seeds ?
rows.solution:
Any two differences:

| Dominant trait | Recessive trait |
|---|---|
| When both the dominant and the recessive trait are inherited, the dominant trait is expressed. | When both are inherited, the recessive trait is not expressed. |
| A single copy of the dominant trait is enough for it to be expressed. | Both copies must be recessive for the trait to be expressed. |

In Mendel's cross, YY \(\times\) yy gives all Yy (yellow) plants in \(\mathrm{F_1}\). Self-pollinating these (Yy \(\times\) Yy) gives YY : Yy : yy = 1 : 2 : 1 in \(\mathrm{F_2}\). YY and Yy both have yellow seeds, so \(\dfrac{3}{4}\), that is 75%, of the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) plants had yellow seeds.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Define the term power of accommodation of human eye. What happens to the image distance in the eye when we increase the distance of an object from the eye ? Name and explain the role of the part of human eye responsible for it in this case.
rows.solution:
Power of accommodation: the ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length.

When the object is moved farther from the eye, the image distance in the eye remains unchanged: the image still forms on the retina.

This is done by the ciliary muscles. While the eye focuses on a distant object, the ciliary muscles relax, the eye lens becomes thinner and its focal length increases, so the image of the distant object still falls on the retina.

rows.stem:
A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board. He places a bar magnet in the centre of it. He sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet. Then he taps the drawing board gently and observes that the iron filings arrange themselves in a particular pattern.

(a) Why do iron filings arrange in a particular pattern ?

(b) What does the crowding of iron filings at the ends of the magnet indicate ?

(c) What do the lines, along which the iron filings align, represent ?

(d) If the student places a cardboard horizontally in a current carrying solenoid and repeats the above activity, in what pattern would the iron filings arrange ? State the conclusion drawn about the magnetic field based on the observed pattern of the lines.
rows.solution:
(a) A magnetic field exists around the bar magnet. Each iron filing becomes a tiny magnet in this field and lines up along the direction of the field, so the filings arrange themselves in a pattern.

(b) The crowding of iron filings at the ends shows that the magnetic field is strongest near the poles of the magnet.

(c) The lines along which the filings align represent the magnetic field lines.

(d) Inside the solenoid the iron filings arrange themselves in equidistant parallel straight lines. This shows that the magnetic field inside the solenoid is uniform (the same at all points).

rows.stem:
Study the picture given below showing three food chains (a), (b) and (c) and answer the following questions :

(i) Name the type of ecosystems that exist in food chains (b) and (c).

(ii) The first trophic level in all food chains are producers. Why ? What percentage of solar energy do these producers capture for their use ?

(iii) Why are the arrows shown in the diagram in one direction only and not vice versa ? Justify.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the three food chains (a), (b) and (c) are given only as a picture of drawn organisms joined by one-way arrows: (a) trees, a deer and a tiger; (b) and (c) are each a column of drawn producers and animals whose identity decides the ecosystem type asked in (i), withheld here. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(i) Food chain (b), grass to grasshopper to frog to snake to eagle, is a terrestrial (grassland) ecosystem. Food chain (c), aquatic plants to a small aquatic animal to fish to a heron, is an aquatic (pond) ecosystem.

(ii) The first trophic level is always made up of producers (autotrophs), because only they can capture solar energy and convert it into chemical energy stored in food, which all the other levels depend on. The green plants capture about 1% of the energy of the sunlight that falls on their leaves.

(iii) The arrows point one way because the flow of energy is in one direction only. The energy that passes from one trophic level to the next cannot come back to the earlier level, so the arrows cannot be reversed.

rows.stem: What is a chemical reaction ? Describe one activity each to show that a chemical change has occurred in which (i) change of colour, and (ii) change in temperature has taken place.
rows.solution:
A chemical reaction is a process in which the reactants change into new substances (products), by the breaking and making of bonds between atoms.

(i) Change of colour: take lead nitrate solution in a test tube and add potassium iodide solution to it. A yellow precipitate of lead iodide forms in the colourless solution.

\(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2 + 2KI \rightarrow PbI_2 + 2KNO_3}\)

Name the yellow colour of the precipitate: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if the colour is not mentioned. (Any other example showing a change of colour is acceptable.)

(ii) Change in temperature: take a small amount of calcium oxide (quick lime) in a beaker and slowly add water to it. It reacts vigorously to form slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), and the beaker becomes hot because a large amount of heat is released.

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

(Any other example showing a change in temperature is acceptable.)

rows.stem:
(i) Define a decomposition reaction. How can we say that (I) electrolysis of water, and (II) blackening of silver bromide when exposed to sunlight, are decomposition reactions ? Mention the type of energy involved in each case.

(ii) “The type of reactions in which (I) calcium oxide is formed, and (II) calcium hydroxide is formed are opposite reactions to each other.” Justify this statement with the help of chemical equations.
rows.solution:
(i) A decomposition reaction is one in which a single reactant breaks down to give two or more simpler products. It needs energy to split the reactant.

(I) In the electrolysis of water, water splits into hydrogen gas and oxygen gas, so it is a decomposition reaction. The energy involved is electrical energy.

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

(II) In sunlight, silver bromide breaks down into silver (which is grey, so the salt blackens) and bromine, so it is a decomposition reaction. The energy involved is light energy.

\(\mathrm{2AgBr(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Br_2(g)}\)

(ii) (I) Calcium oxide is formed by heating calcium carbonate. This is a decomposition reaction, and it absorbs heat (endothermic):

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

(II) Calcium hydroxide is formed when calcium oxide combines with water. This is a combination reaction, and it releases heat (exothermic):

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

One reaction breaks a substance down and absorbs heat, the other joins substances together and releases heat, so they are opposite types of reactions.

rows.stem:
(i) Define a reflex arc. Why have reflex arcs evolved in animals ? Trace the sequence of events which occur, when you suddenly touch a hot object.

(ii) Name the part of nervous system which helps in communication between the central nervous system and other parts of the body. What are the two components of this system ?
rows.solution:
(i) The pathway along which nerve impulses travel during a reflex action is called a reflex arc.

Reflex arcs have evolved because the thinking part of the brain is not fast enough. A quick response is needed to avoid injury, and the connection in the spinal cord gives that response without waiting for the brain.

Sequence of events on touching a hot object: hot object (stimulus) \(\rightarrow\) receptors in the skin \(\rightarrow\) sensory neuron \(\rightarrow\) spinal cord \(\rightarrow\) motor neuron \(\rightarrow\) effector (muscles of the arm) \(\rightarrow\) response: the hand is pulled away.

(ii) The peripheral nervous system. Its two components are the cranial nerves (arising from the brain) and the spinal nerves (arising from the spinal cord).

rows.stem:
(i) Leaves of ‘chhui-mui’ plant begin to fold up and droop in response to a stimulus. Name the stimulus and write the cause for such a rapid movement. Is there any growth involved in the movement ?

(ii) Define geotropism in plants. What is meant by positive and negative geotropism ? Give one example of each type.
rows.solution:
(i) The stimulus is touch.

The movement is rapid because the plant cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them. The information about the touch passes from cell to cell by electrical-chemical means, and the cells at the base of the leaves shrink as they lose water, so the leaves fold up and droop.

No growth is involved in this movement.

(ii) Geotropism is the growth of a part of a plant in response to the pull of the earth, that is, to gravity.

Positive geotropism: growth of a plant part towards gravity. Example: roots grow downwards.

Negative geotropism: growth of a plant part away from gravity. Example: shoots grow upwards.

rows.stem:
The variation of image distance (v) with object distance (u) for a convex lens is given in the following observation table. Analyse it and answer the questions that follow :

| S. No. | Object distance (u) cm | Image distance (v) cm |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | \(-150\) | \(+30\) |
| 2 | \(-75\) | \(+37{\cdot}5\) |
| 3 | \(-50\) | \(+50\) |
| 4 | \(-37{\cdot}5\) | \(+75\) |
| 5 | \(-30\) | \(+150\) |
| 6 | \(-15\) | \(+37{\cdot}5\) |

(i) Without calculation, find the focal length of the convex lens. Justify your answer.

(ii) Which observation is not correct ? Why ? Draw ray diagram to find the position of the image formed for this position of the object.

(iii) Find the approximate value of magnification for \(u = -30\) cm.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: in (iii) the magnification is printed as \(-5\) cm. Magnification is a ratio of two distances, so it has no unit; the value is \(-5\).]

(i) In observation 3 the object distance and the image distance are equal (50 cm each). For a convex lens this happens only when the object is at 2F, so \(2f = 50\) cm and the focal length is \(f = 25\) cm.

(ii) Observation 6 is not correct. There the object (15 cm) is between the optical centre and the focus (25 cm), so the image is virtual, erect and on the same side of the lens as the object; the image distance must be negative. (By the lens formula, \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{15} = -\dfrac{2}{75}\), so \(v = -37{\cdot}5\) cm.)

Ray diagram: place the object AB between \(\mathrm{F_1}\) and the optical centre O. From A draw a ray parallel to the principal axis, which after refraction passes through \(\mathrm{F_2}\), and a ray through O, which goes straight on. The two refracted rays diverge, so produce them backwards with dotted lines: they meet at A' on the same side as the object, beyond \(\mathrm{F_1}\). The image A'B' is virtual, erect and enlarged. Draw arrows on the rays: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if the direction of the rays is not shown.

(iii) For \(u = -30\) cm the table gives \(v = +150\) cm, so

\(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{+150}{-30} = -5\).

The image is real, inverted and five times the size of the object.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
(i) Define principal axis of a lens. Draw a ray diagram to show what happens when a ray of light parallel to the principal axis of a concave lens passes through it.

(ii) The focal length of a concave lens is 20 cm. At what distance from the lens should a 5 cm tall object be placed so that its image is formed at a distance of 15 cm from the lens ? Also calculate the size of the image formed.
rows.solution:
(i) The principal axis of a lens is the imaginary straight line passing through the two centres of curvature of its surfaces.

Ray diagram: draw a concave lens with its principal axis and mark \(\mathrm{F_1}\) on the side the light comes from and \(\mathrm{F_2}\) on the other side. A ray parallel to the principal axis, after passing through the lens, diverges (bends away from the axis). Produce the refracted ray backwards with a dotted line: it appears to come from the principal focus \(\mathrm{F_1}\) on the same side as the incident ray. Draw arrows on the rays.

(ii) For a concave lens \(f = -20\) cm. The image of a concave lens is virtual and on the object's side, so \(v = -15\) cm, and \(h = 5\) cm.

By the lens formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-15} - \dfrac{1}{-20} = \dfrac{-4 + 3}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{60}\), so \(u = -60\) cm.

The object should be placed 60 cm from the lens.

Size of the image: \(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = \dfrac{v}{u}\), so \(h' = \dfrac{v}{u} \times h = \dfrac{-15}{-60} \times 5 = 1{\cdot}25\) cm.

The image is 1.25 cm tall, erect (positive height), virtual and diminished.

rows.stem: When activity was done with dilute hydrochloric acid, then in which one of the test tubes was the rate of formation of bubbles the fastest and the thermometer showed the highest temperature ?
rows.context: Three metal samples of magnesium, aluminium and iron were taken and rubbed with sand paper. These samples were then put separately in test tubes containing dilute hydrochloric acid. Thermometers were also suspended in each test tube so that their bulbs dipped in the acid. The rate of formation of bubbles was observed. The above activity was repeated with dilute nitric acid and the observations were recorded.
rows.solution: In the test tube containing magnesium. Magnesium is the most reactive of the three metals, so it reacts fastest with the acid, giving bubbles of hydrogen most rapidly and releasing the most heat.

rows.stem: Which metal did not react with dilute hydrochloric acid ? Give reason.
rows.context: Three metal samples of magnesium, aluminium and iron were taken and rubbed with sand paper. These samples were then put separately in test tubes containing dilute hydrochloric acid. Thermometers were also suspended in each test tube so that their bulbs dipped in the acid. The rate of formation of bubbles was observed. The above activity was repeated with dilute nitric acid and the observations were recorded.
rows.solution:
All three metals, magnesium, aluminium and iron, react with dilute hydrochloric acid, because they are all more reactive than hydrogen and can displace it from the acid. So none of the three failed to react.

The marking scheme also gives the marks for naming a metal less reactive than hydrogen, such as copper, with the reason that it lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series and so cannot displace hydrogen from the acid.

rows.stem: Why is hydrogen gas not evolved when a metal reacts with dilute nitric acid ? Name the ultimate products formed in the reaction.
rows.context: Three metal samples of magnesium, aluminium and iron were taken and rubbed with sand paper. These samples were then put separately in test tubes containing dilute hydrochloric acid. Thermometers were also suspended in each test tube so that their bulbs dipped in the acid. The rate of formation of bubbles was observed. The above activity was repeated with dilute nitric acid and the observations were recorded.
rows.solution:
Hydrogen gas is not evolved because nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen produced to water, and is itself reduced to oxides of nitrogen (such as \(\mathrm{N_2O}\), NO or \(\mathrm{NO_2}\)).

The ultimate products are water and oxides of nitrogen (along with the nitrate of the metal).

rows.stem: Name the type of reaction on the basis of which reactivity of metals is decided. You have two metals X and Y. How would you decide which is more reactive than the other ?
rows.context: Three metal samples of magnesium, aluminium and iron were taken and rubbed with sand paper. These samples were then put separately in test tubes containing dilute hydrochloric acid. Thermometers were also suspended in each test tube so that their bulbs dipped in the acid. The rate of formation of bubbles was observed. The above activity was repeated with dilute nitric acid and the observations were recorded.
rows.solution:
The reactivity of metals is decided on the basis of displacement reactions.

To compare X and Y, put a piece of metal X in a solution of a salt of Y. If X displaces Y from its salt solution (Y is deposited and the solution changes), X is more reactive than Y. If no reaction takes place, Y is more reactive; this can be confirmed by putting Y in a solution of a salt of X, when Y will displace X.

rows.stem:
(i) Name the artery that brings oxygenated blood to the kidney.

(ii) Name the cluster the thin-walled blood capillaries present in the Bowman’s capsule.
rows.context: Kidneys are vital organs for survival. Several factors like infections, injury or restricted blood flow to kidneys reduce the activity of kidneys. This leads to accumulation of poisonous wastes in the body, which can even lead to death. In case of kidney failure, an artificial kidney can be used. An artificial kidney is a device to remove waste products from the blood through dialysis.
rows.solution:
(i) The renal artery.

(ii) The glomerulus.

rows.stem: In human excretory system name the organ which stores urine. Is this organ under hormonal control or nervous control ?
rows.context: Kidneys are vital organs for survival. Several factors like infections, injury or restricted blood flow to kidneys reduce the activity of kidneys. This leads to accumulation of poisonous wastes in the body, which can even lead to death. In case of kidney failure, an artificial kidney can be used. An artificial kidney is a device to remove waste products from the blood through dialysis.
rows.solution: The urinary bladder stores urine. It is muscular, and it is under nervous control: we can usually control the urge to pass urine.

rows.stem: List two major steps involved in the formation of urine and state in brief their functions.
rows.context: Kidneys are vital organs for survival. Several factors like infections, injury or restricted blood flow to kidneys reduce the activity of kidneys. This leads to accumulation of poisonous wastes in the body, which can even lead to death. In case of kidney failure, an artificial kidney can be used. An artificial kidney is a device to remove waste products from the blood through dialysis.
rows.solution:
Filtration: in the glomerulus, the blood is filtered into Bowman's capsule, and nitrogenous wastes such as urea or uric acid are removed from the blood.

Reabsorption: as the filtrate passes along the tubule, useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts and a major amount of water are selectively reabsorbed into the blood.

rows.stem: In which part of the nephron does selective reabsorption take place ? List the factors which the amount of water reabsorbed depends on.
rows.context: Kidneys are vital organs for survival. Several factors like infections, injury or restricted blood flow to kidneys reduce the activity of kidneys. This leads to accumulation of poisonous wastes in the body, which can even lead to death. In case of kidney failure, an artificial kidney can be used. An artificial kidney is a device to remove waste products from the blood through dialysis.
rows.solution:
Selective reabsorption takes place in the tubular part of the nephron.

The amount of water reabsorbed depends on how much excess water there is in the body, and on how much dissolved waste has to be excreted.

rows.stem: Find the value of total resistance between the points A and B.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit is given only as a drawing: points A, B and C, resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 16 Ω, two 8 Ω resistors, a 6 V battery and a key; which resistors lie between A and B, which between B and C, and how each group is connected decide every answer and are withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
Between A and B the \(4\,\Omega\), \(6\,\Omega\) and \(16\,\Omega\) resistors are in series:

\(R_s = 4 + 6 + 16 = 26\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Find the resistance between the points B and C.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit is given only as a drawing: points A, B and C, resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 16 Ω, two 8 Ω resistors, a 6 V battery and a key; which resistors lie between A and B, which between B and C, and how each group is connected decide every answer and are withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
Between B and C the two \(8\,\Omega\) resistors are in parallel:

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}\), so \(R_p = 4\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Calculate the current drawn from the battery, when the key is closed.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit is given only as a drawing: points A, B and C, resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 16 Ω, two 8 Ω resistors, a 6 V battery and a key; which resistors lie between A and B, which between B and C, and how each group is connected decide every answer and are withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
The two sections are in series, so the total resistance is \(26 + 4 = 30\,\Omega\).

With \(V = 6\) V, the current drawn from the battery is \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6}{30} = \dfrac{1}{5}\) A, that is \(0{\cdot}2\) A.

rows.stem: In the above circuit, the \(16\,\Omega\) resistor or the parallel combination of two resistors of \(8\,\Omega\), which one of the two will have more potential difference across its two ends ? Justify your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit is given only as a drawing: points A, B and C, resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 16 Ω, two 8 Ω resistors, a 6 V battery and a key; which resistors lie between A and B, which between B and C, and how each group is connected decide every answer and are withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
The \(16\,\Omega\) resistor has the greater potential difference across it.

The total resistance of the circuit is \(4 + 6 + 16 + 4 = 30\,\Omega\), so the current is \(I = \dfrac{6}{30} = 0{\cdot}2\) A, and the same current flows through the \(16\,\Omega\) resistor and through the parallel combination (\(4\,\Omega\)). By Ohm's law, for the same current the potential difference is greater across the greater resistance:

across the \(16\,\Omega\) resistor, \(V = IR = 0{\cdot}2 \times 16 = 3{\cdot}2\) V;

across the parallel combination, \(V = IR_p = 0{\cdot}2 \times 4 = 0{\cdot}8\) V.
